A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DisCoVR study and contain readable main text and Appendices A–H. Methods, equations, proofs, experiments, tables, and figures can be matched despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original quantitative and qualitative experiments on synthetic data, colored MNIST, CelebA glasses and hats, and lupus single-cell RNA-sequencing data.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments, reports revised single-cell results, and adds adversarial-weight sensitivity results in Appendix F.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects the encoder/decoder update from gradient descent to ascent, matching the retained max–min objective. Appendix H.1.5 also changes the stated single-cell implementation from avoiding a prior network to using a network-parametrized prior. The central dual-latent architecture and objective remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same parametric model, noisy Swiss Roll, colored MNIST noise conditions, CelebA glasses and hats, and lupus single-cell data. CelebA-Hats already appears in v2 Appendix G; the added weight sweep introduces no new dataset or task scenario.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same methods, including CVAE in image visualizations and CSVAE/HCSVAE variants, DIVA, and CCVAE in the matched tables. The change from N.A. to No Adv. is a renaming.

E3.justification: Appendix F adds an adversarial-weight sweep over 0, 2, 4, 6, and 8 using existing information metrics. Appendix H.1.5 replaces v2's explicit 10-dimensional w exception with a neural prior under the stated z=10, w=2 setup, although v3's phrase 'matched sizes' leaves the dimensional description imperfectly clear.

E4.justification: v2 already examines classifying directly from z and replacing the conditional prior with a standard Gaussian. v3 retains these analyses and adds a targeted study of sensitivity to adversarial strength on noisy Swiss Roll, reported with kNN and MINE estimates in Appendix F, Tables 12–13.

E5.justification: Both Appendix H.1 passages specify 10 repetitions with different random seeds and reporting means and standard deviations. No new statistical testing or uncertainty-estimation procedure is introduced. The added weight-sweep tables provide point estimates without additional run information.

E6.justification: Appendix F adds weight-sweep results. In v2 Supplementary Table 17 versus v3 Appendix Table 19, DisCoVR's w-stimulation NMI changes from 0.946±0.002 to 0.906±0.003, and z-cell-type NMI from 0.688±0.0 to 0.716±0.031. Its single-cell visualization is also revised. Because the stated configuration changes, these are replaced results rather than established same-setting gains. Other existing tables retain their values.

T1.justification: Appendix B.2.2 corrects the signs of the q(w|x,y) entropy integral and expected log-posterior term in the negative-KL expansion: v2 Equations 27–28 become v3 Equations 26–27. The propositions and regularity conditions otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

C1.justification: The overall disentanglement and unique-equilibrium claims remain. However, v3's introduction adds a categorical claim that class-wise coupling prevents leakage from w into z, beyond v2's leakage-reduction motivation. The rewritten abstract also inconsistently claims that condition-specific information is removed from the condition-specific representation.

C2.justification: Section 2.4 adds a mechanism argument that class-wise aggregation and the absence of w and y from q(z|x) prevent leakage from w. Section 5.2.2 newly acknowledges the adversarial classifier's higher computational cost on CelebA; v2 supplied runtime measurements without this explicit qualification.

D1.justification: Appendix H.1 replaces the statement that code is attached and will become public upon acceptance with a specific repository link and reported public availability. Appendix H.1.5 revises the single-cell prior implementation description. Most hardware, optimization, architecture, and hyperparameter information is retained.

R1.justification: Section 4 separates the DIVA and CCVAE discussions, adds specific criticisms of missing adversarial enforcement and CCVAE's label-dependent z prior, and revises the independence-based comparison. The Pan et al. transfer-learning survey is removed. The broader related-work coverage in Appendix A remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution narrative, comparison discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten, with further editing throughout the main text. Acknowledgements and an impact statement are added. Editing also introduces inconsistent invariant/condition-specific terminology in the abstract, Figure 5 caption, and Appendix A.1.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column main layout and extensively rearranges and resizes displays. v2 Figure 1 is split into v3 Figures 1–2; MNIST and CelebA grids are reorganized; the single-cell figure is revised; and two ablation tables are added. Appendix displays are broadly reflowed and relabeled.

improvement.justification: Corrected optimization and proof signs, the added sensitivity study, and reported public code access improve correctness, empirical support, and reproducibility. However, v3 introduces role reversals in an abstract that previously distinguished the latent factors correctly, repeats this confusion in Figure 5, and leaves its revised single-cell dimensional description ambiguous. These practical gains and central explanatory regressions prevent a confident net quality judgment.
